Valuing and investing in biodiversity internationally for national security at home
items.summary: This article was first published on the Gov.uk website. Earlier this week Defra’s Minister for Nature, Jenny Riddell-Carpenter, announced £28 million of funding to help support countries in the global south to develop their economies without harming biodiversity, and to invest in their own natural capital. And today at COP17, Minister Riddell-Carpenter hosted an event discussing how to move beyond the conceptual case for nature security, to showcase implementation in practice.

items.title: UK Government and FSD Africa partner to unlock investment for women-led businesses in Nigeria
items.summary: USD 335,000 investment will help Rising Tide Africa bring women entrepreneurs and investors together, with the aim of attracting USD 2.7 million over the next three years. Lagos, Nigeria, 28 October 2026. FSD Africa, with funding from the UK Government through the British High Commission in Nigeria, has committed US$335,000 (approximately £247,000) to establish the RiTA Investment Network, a new platform designed to increase investment in women-led businesses in Nigeria. items.title: Indian PV at a turning point
items.summary: India’s module manufacturing capacity has expanded at remarkable speed, while domestic content requirements are pushing investment into the more complex cell manufacturing sector. Suppliers are also eyeing moves into wafer and ingot manufacturing ahead of further expansion to the domestic content rules. Activity has been more limited in polysilicon manufacturing, as with the development of facilities to produce solar glass and other bill of materials components. items.title: Côte d’Ivoire solar plants: who is behind the 152MWp launched in three days?
items.summary: Côte d’Ivoire’s energy minister, Mamadou Sangafowa-Coulibaly, laid foundation stones for 152MWp of solar in the north of the country between 22 and 24 October, from a Katiola plant whose lenders are due to close financing within weeks to plants led by Ivorian capital at M’Bengué and by the Emirati group AMEA Power at Binguébougou. “We led the negotiations, which were not easy, it has to be said,” Mamadou Sangafowa-Coulibaly said on 22 October at Lonankaha, near Katiola, as he laid the foundation stone of a 50MWp plant for Katiola Solar Power.

items.title: Turning South African Sunshine into Business Power: A BSLBATT C&I Installation
items.summary: A commercial solar and battery storage system installed by ASB Energy combines BSLBATT high-voltage batteries, Sunsynk hybrid inverters and Trina Solar PV modules — bringing together the key components of a modern energy storage solution. Making More of Solar Energy For businesses across South Africa, solar power is an increasingly important part of the energy mix. But generating electricity is only one part of the equation. How that energy is stored, managed and used can be just as important.
